text:
Ryan Shea is the surprise of Edmonton's blue line. A fourth-round pick who didn't reach the NHL until his mid-20s and played 150 games in Pittsburgh, he's now logging 23 minutes a night for the Oilers, more than anyone would have guessed in September.

Evolving-Hockey made the case for him: 3.3 wins above replacement last season, fifth among 215 defencemen, though with a warning that his results ran ahead of his chances (1.9 expected wins). This season he's been steady rather than spectacular. Edmonton takes 52% of the expected goals with him on, about five points better than without him, and his five points in 19 games sit below what his talent range suggests. Our wins-added numbers rank him near the bottom because his points haven't swung games. A big minute-eater who keeps the puck out of trouble is worth plenty on a team built around two forwards who score at will. The question is whether 23 minutes is the right job or just the job that was available.
